subject: Static Topologies
significance: This architectural choice simplifies system modeling, formal verification, and debugging, reducing unforeseen emergent unsafe behaviors and attack surface.

subject: Adaptive Conditional Routing
significance: This paradigm shifts from 'brittle predictability' by enabling dynamic pathway adjustment and real-time component bypass to circumvent failures and threats, ensuring operational continuity.

subject: Conditional Determinism
significance: It allows adaptive systems to maintain safety assurances within an otherwise dynamic framework, bridging the gap between adaptability and reliability.

subject: Distributed Consensus-Based Routing
significance: This approach significantly increases the difficulty of compromising multiple routing decision points compared to centralized static systems.

subject: Computational Overhead of Adaptive Routing
significance: It is justified by the potentially catastrophic costs of failure in static systems when operating in highly unpredictable conditions, prioritizing resilience over simplicity.
